question: Will William Lawrence be the Democratic nominee for MI-07?
rules:
This market will resolve according to the candidate who wins the nomination for the Democratic Party to contest the MI-07 congressional district seat in the U.S. House of Representatives in the 2026 midterm elections. The Democratic primary will take place on August 4, 2026.

If no nominee is announced by November 3, 2026, 11:59 PM ET, this market will resolve to "Other".

The resolution source for this market will be a consensus of official Democrat sources, including https://democrats.org/.

Any replacement of the nominee before election day will not change the resolution of the market.

evidence.excerpt: U.S. Senator Elissa Slotkin, the last Democrat to represent Michigan’s 7th Congressional District, announced her endorsement of Matt Maasdam for Congress, backing the retired Navy SEAL. Maasdam has earned labor union endorsements including the Michigan Pipe Trades Association, IBEW Michigan, Teamsters Local 243, and the Michigan Professional Fire Fighters Union.

Lawrence has been on top in most available polls, including in an internal poll from one of his two Democratic primary opponents, ex-Navy SEAL and business executive Matt Maasdam. A third poll sponsored by his other opponent, former U.S. Ambassador to Ukraine Bridget Brink, has her out in front. Maasdam is being boosted by a $750,000 VoteVets ad campaign, while National Nurses United has invested $400,000 in a super PAC for Lawrence.

Respondents were first asked which candidate they would support if the election were held today. Lawrence held a narrow lead with 5.9%, compared to 4.9% for Bridget Brink and 3.8% for Matt Maasdam, with most voters undecided. After hearing a brief biography of the three candidates, Lawrence came out with 45.2% support to Maasdam's 11.7% and Brink’s 9.9% in the March 17–18 survey.
